newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe shares end soft, further slipping seen.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe shares end soft, further slipping seen.

text.p: Zimbabwe industrial shares surprised nobody by finishing Thursday weaker and are likely to extend their fall although no plunge is seen, dealers said.
"The trend was very much softer today and this was not unexpected and is likely to continue," one trader said.

Unlike Tuesday and Wednesday when stocks were overall mixed, industrial counters were mostly down but dealers said that the market's fundamentals -- which had awarded it a bull run earlier -- remain positive.
"It was not as mixed as it was previously, but genuinely down. Still, it remains fairly well underpinned and no dramatic fall is expected," one dealer said.
Dealers added that investors are likely to let stocks soften a bit more before coming in to snap up bargains.

The 57-counter industrial index lost 62.37 points to 10,164.16. FMB lost 150 cents to 6,250, Natfoods shed 60 cents to 600, Zimpapers cut 50 cents to 2,900, BAT was off 50 cents to 2,100 and Finhold shed 10 cents to 780 cents.

Dealers said that the seven-share mining index would hold little allure for investors as long as the gold price remained dull. But Ashanti scored 500 cents to 10,000 on mostly one purchase and traders said that that buyer was still in the market for more.
The mining index inched up 1.76 points to 970.35 points -- barely rescuing itself from its 29-month low on Wednesday.
Falgold, MCM and Rio Tinto were unchanged.
Dealers said that overall volumes had been average with a lot of small shares trading and most activity in one-off orders.
They said that institutions had been very quiet.
